was: Chickasaw Nation-operated public park 11 mi W of Atoka then 4 mi S; year-round drive-in tent/RV camping (rigs to 50 ft) across 35 wooded acres, 30-amp electric and electric/water sites, water/showers/dump, fishing lake, nature trails, disc golf. FCFS / call park office. --Claude

was: City of Sayre park: ~80 RV sites with 30/50-amp, pull-thru sites + one handicap pad, on-site dump station; $12 honor-system, first-come first-served. Set amid a 9-hole golf course, pool and fishing ponds, just off US-283 near I-40. --Claude

was: Cleveland County Fairgrounds RV park in Norman: 35 full-hookup + 10 water/electric 50-amp sites, first-come first-served; operates year-round (may be unavailable during major fairground events). --Claude

was: Town of Gore riverside park on the lower Illinois River (Arkansas River tailwater below Tenkiller dam). 10 drive-in RV sites w/ water + 30-amp electric plus 12 tent sites; boat ramp. First-come, first-served, small nightly fee. --Claude

was: City of Chickasha (Parks & Rec) lake in Grady County near Verden. Lakeside primitive campsites plus RV hookup sites (electric/water); restrooms w/ showers, three boat ramps, fishing docks. First-come, first-served w/ envelope payment; rigs to ~32 ft. --Claude
note: City of Chickasha (Parks & Rec) lake in Grady County near Verden. Lakeside primitive campsites plus RV hookup sites (electric/water); restrooms, three boat ramps, fishing docks. Envelope payment. --Claude

was: CCC-era developed recreation complex in the Winn Ranger District of Kisatchie NF; drive-in campground with picnic tables, lantern posts and fire rings, restroom, no hookups; $10/night, first-come, first-served (scan-and-pay via rec.gov app). Small Gum Springs Lake and short hiking trails adjacent; a separate horse camp is nearby. --Claude

was: Calcasieu Ranger District; 14 drive-in sites (6 along the 46-acre Valentine Lake) with paved pads (narrow, some crumbling — small/mid RVs, though reviewers report fitting 20+ ft rigs), picnic table/lantern post/fire ring, flush toilets, community water spigots, no hookups; $10/night, first-come, first-served. The South Shore across the lake is day-use only (8a-8p). Wild Azalea Trail access. --Claude

was: Primitive hunter camp in the Red Dirt Wildlife Management Preserve (Kisatchie Ranger District), drive-in off a forest road; essentially an open field with room for RVs and tents, toilet and picnic tables, no potable water, no hookups; usable year-round, first-come, first-served. --Claude

was: Primitive camp in the Vernon Unit (Calcasieu Ranger District), reached via LA-10 and Vernon Parish Road 443; two dispersed camping loops with vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups; self-contained RVs and tents, first-come, first-served; pack-in/pack-out. --Claude

was: Developed USFS campground on Fullerton Lake at the historic Fullerton Sawmill/Mill site (Calcasieu RD, Vernon Unit); ~8 sites (tent & RV), new bathhouse with hot showers & flush toilets, potable water, non-motorized boat launch. First-come, first-served, $15/night (rec.gov scan-and-pay). NOTE: USFS lists camping temporarily closed as of 2026 (day-use/boat launch remain open). --Claude

NOTE: USFS lists camping temporarily closed as of 2026 (day-use/boat launch remain open). --Claude

was: Primitive USFS hunter/horse & general camp inside the Red Dirt WMA (Kisatchie RD); large open clearing off gravel Forest Rd 311 (reached via paved Longleaf Trail FH 59), vault toilets, no water, first-come, first-served. --Claude

was: Primitive USFS hunter camp off US-167 at the Catahoula WMA (Catahoula RD); open clearing with vault toilet, no potable water, pack-in/pack-out, first-come, first-served. Easy drive-in access from the highway; heavy pine canopy. --Claude

was: Developed 8-site campground on 5-acre Stuart Lake in Kisatchie NF (Catahoula RD), sites renovated 2009; drinking water, restrooms, drive-in sites. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay via the rec.gov app), $15/single site. --Claude

was: Caddo Parish 40-acre park on Caddo Lake: RV sites with water + 50-amp electric ($12) plus primitive sites ($6), public boat ramp, 450-ft fishing pier, swimming area. Cash only, first-come first-served (no reservations), 14-day limit. --Claude
note: Caddo Parish 40-acre park on Caddo Lake: RV sites with water + 50-amp electric ($12) plus primitive sites ($6), public boat ramp, 450-ft fishing pier, swimming area. Cash only. --Claude

was: Drive-on Gulf of Mexico beach dispersed camping on Bolivar Peninsula, reached via Rettilon Rd; compacted sand is drivable by normal vehicles and RVs park above the tide line. Dry camping only (one pit toilet), first-come first-served. A ~$10 Galveston County beach parking/camping permit is required on the east/right stretch; a short free stretch lies west/left. --Claude

was: TPWD park above the 84,000-acre Falcon International Reservoir (Rio Grande). 98 drive-in sites in three loops: Javelina Run (31 full-hookup pull-throughs, 30/50-amp), Mesquite Bend (31 water+electric pull-throughs) and Black Bass (36 water-only, non-reservable/FCFS). Screened shelters and cabins also available; dump station, restrooms with showers. Reservable online. --Claude

Screened shelters and cabins also available; restrooms. Reservable online. --Claude

was: Primitive/dispersed camping on Hubbard Creek Reservoir, managed by the West Central Texas Municipal Water District (member cities Abilene, Albany, Anson, Breckenridge). Open cleared shoreline areas easily reached by normal vehicle with room for rigs of all sizes, plus a couple of trash cans/portable toilets; the North Park also has 2 FCFS RV hookups. --Claude

was: First-come, first-served dispersed camping around Millers Creek Reservoir (2,212 acres), owned by the North Central Texas Municipal Water Authority. No hookups; boat ramp with restrooms/dumpster. Paved approach on the dam/north side reaches maintained waterfront pull-offs where a 23-ft rig fits (reviewers parked 23-ft and 33-ft rigs at the water); interior tracks are dirt and can be impassable when wet. --Claude

was: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area primitive campground off US-277 north of the reservoir. 17 first-come, first-served sites for RVs or tents; no hookups and no potable water, with pit toilets, picnic tables and fire grills. RVs/trailers over 36 ft cannot be accommodated. --Claude
note: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area primitive campground off US-277 north of the reservoir. 17 sites for RVs or tents, with picnic tables and fire grills. --Claude

was: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area limited-development campground on a peninsula off US-90. 15 gravel sites for tents or RVs, all first-come, first-served; no hookups but potable water available, restrooms/vault toilets and a picnic shelter. RV length limit 28 ft (fits a 23-ft rig). --Claude
note: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area limited-development campground on a peninsula off US-90. 15 gravel sites for tents or RVs; restrooms and a picnic shelter. --Claude

was: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area primitive campground at Rough Canyon on the edge of Amistad Reservoir. 4 first-come, first-served sites for tents or RVs, each with a covered picnic table and grill; flush toilets and a boat ramp on-site. --Claude
note: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area primitive campground at Rough Canyon on the edge of Amistad Reservoir. 4 sites for tents or RVs, each with a covered picnic table and grill; a boat ramp on-site. --Claude

was: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area primitive campground in the San Pedro area off US-90. 30 first-come, first-served sites for RVs or tents plus 5 tent-only sites; primitive, no hookups. --Claude

was: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area primitive campground on Spur 406 off US-90. 6 first-come, first-served sites for RVs or tents; no hookups and no potable water, with pit toilets and trash cans. RVs/trailers over 30 ft cannot be accommodated. --Claude
note: NPS Amistad National Recreation Area primitive campground on Spur 406 off US-90. 6 sites for RVs or tents, with trash cans. --Claude

was: NPS Padre Island National Seashore campground on the Laguna Madre bay side. 35 side-by-side gravel RV/tent sites (20+ fit big rigs, no hookups) plus 10 tent-only sites; vault toilets, no water/electric. First-come, first-served, $8/night; open year-round. Popular windsurfing/kayaking spot. --Claude

was: USFS Sabine National Forest campground in the northern district near the historic fox-hound cemetery. 20 sites with electric and water hookups; self-pay fee station, amphitheater and group shelter (day-use). Horses allowed in the campground. Open year-round, first-come, first-served. --Claude
note: USFS Sabine National Forest campground in the northern district near the historic fox-hound cemetery. 20 sites with electric and water hookups; self-pay fee station, amphitheater and group shelter (day-use). Horses allowed in the campground. --Claude

was: USFS Angelina National Forest campground on Boykin Springs Lake. Standard tent/RV sites plus a few tent-only; 9 RV sites accommodate trailers up to 24 ft. Drinking water, flush toilets and hot showers; no hookups. First-come, first-served, $10/site (up to 2 vehicles); group shelter reservable. Sawmill Trail to the Aldridge Sawmill starts here. --Claude

was: USFWS refuge SSW of Umbarger (entrance 1.5 mi south on FM 168, last ~2 mi packed dirt). Primitive drive-in camping at Cottonwood Canyon below the old dam; ~10+ dispersed sites, no hookups and no water (the lake itself has been dry for decades), vault restrooms and picnic tables, trash dumpster. Sites fit large rigs (reviewers report 40-ft+). Free with America the Beautiful pass, 7-night limit, first-come first-served. Automatic gates close 8pm (6pm Oct-Mar) and open 8am. --Claude

was: USFS Angelina National Forest recreation area on a point of Sam Rayburn Reservoir (off FM 2743, SE of Zavalla). 26 drive-in sites with picnic tables, fire rings and lantern posts; primitive -- no hookups and no drinking water/trash service; boat ramp. Drive-in access for RVs up to 48 ft. First-come first-served (scan-and-pay via the Recreation.gov app on site). --Claude

was: NPS Big Bend National Park mountain campground in the Chisos Basin at ~5,400 ft; ~60 sites, no hookups, dump station, flush toilets. The access road is steep and winding with sharp switchbacks — NPS discourages trailers over 20 ft and RVs over 24 ft; a 23-ft rig fits with caution and sites are small/rocky/unlevel. Reservable online year-round (no first-come, first-served). --Claude

was: USFS Caddo/LBJ National Grasslands, ~17 mi N of Honey Grove on Coffee Mill Lake. 13 first-come, first-served drive-in sites with picnic tables, fire rings, potable water and vault toilets; boat ramp and fishing pier on the lake. Sites suit tents and small-to-mid RVs (loop road with pull-offs, room for slideouts). --Claude

was: Dispersed FCFS boondocking on FR 904 in the Lyndon B. Johnson National Grassland, ~30 min from Decatur. Hard-packed gravel road; a ridge loop with several widely spaced clearings — a couple fit larger RVs (firsthand reviews report 32–40 ft rigs). Reach it via CR 2461 (GPS routing over CR 2474 dead-ends at a closed gate). No hookups or services; 14-day limit. --Claude

was: USFS Sabine National Forest recreation area on Toledo Bend Reservoir, operated by the Sabine River Authority of Texas. 37 drive-in travel-trailer/tent sites (no hookups), each with fire ring and picnic table; portable toilets, two boat ramps and a fishing pier. First-come first-served (not on recreation.gov). Access via FM 3382 to Forest Service Rd 130. --Claude

was: USFS McClellan Creek National Grassland (Cibola NF) in the Texas Panhandle prairie, by Lake McClellan (a drought-prone reservoir that is frequently dry) -- RV Life lists it as 'McDowell Campground.' ~60 units, roughly half with water/electric and the rest primitive; bathhouse with hot showers, dump station, group shelter, camp host. The grassland's only RV campground. First-come, first-served self-pay; not on recreation.gov. --Claude

was: Privately-operated marina/RV park (concessionaire, under new ownership) on the south shore of Lake Somerville near the dam, Brenham. Full-hookup RV sites with wide pull-throughs plus additional electric/water sites and cabins; full-service marina with boat slips, ramp and fuel; open year-round to transient campers. Book direct (not on recreation.gov). RV Life unrated/$ ; basics confirmed from operator site (auto 6/2026). --Claude

was: NPS Padre Island National Seashore developed campground behind the dunes at Malaquite Beach. 48 sites total: 24 paved and 18 ocean-side sites open to tents AND RVs (6 more are tent-only). No hookups; cold-water rinse showers, restrooms, picnic tables/shade shelters, with potable water and dump station on the road in. First-come, first-served (self-registration kiosk); $14/night, park entrance/annual pass required. --Claude

Flush toilets, showers, drinking water, dump station, boat ramp, playground; Hopewell Trail trailhead. Swim area, picnic areas, amphitheater; open year-round. Reservable online. --Claude

First-come, first-served (pay on site via Recreation.gov app). --Claude

was: USFS Angelina National Forest developed recreation area at road's end on the south shore of Sam Rayburn Reservoir near Zavalla; drive-in tent and RV sites (no hookups), cold showers, boat ramp. First-come, first-served (~$10); not on recreation.gov. --Claude

was: USACE (Fort Worth District) primitive park on the shore of Lake Whitney just south of Morgan. 21 camp/picnic sites with ground cookers, no hookups; two vault-toilet restrooms, water faucets, two boat ramps. Drive-in sites strung along the shoreline road. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude
